title: Hagestad & Settersten (2017): Multiple Choice
instructions: Choose the single answer most accurately supported by the reading.

items.prompt: Which statement best captures the essay's central argument?
options: Aging differences arise only from genes and individual lifestyle
Aging is interpersonal, shaped by relationships, policy, and history
Later-life networks universally shrink independently of social conditions
Successful aging requires full-time employment and complete independence
items.answer: Aging is interpersonal, shaped by relationships, policy, and history
items.explanation: The autobiographies place interdependent lives and social conditions at the center of understanding aging.

items.prompt: What kind of evidence does the essay primarily develop?
options: A national panel estimating the causal effect of migration on health
A clinical case report diagnosing two migrants
A cross-national cost-effectiveness review of caregiving policies
A reflective interpretation of two autobiographies using social theory
items.answer: A reflective interpretation of two autobiographies using social theory
items.explanation: The stories make mechanisms and questions visible; they do not estimate population frequencies or average causal effects.

items.prompt: What analytical possibility does the stranger's position offer?
options: Questioning familiar rules from both inside and outside
Defining every social boundary exclusively by nationality
Following local rules more accurately by losing all shared meanings
Achieving complete objectivity through total absence of relationships
items.answer: Questioning familiar rules from both inside and outside
items.explanation: Combining nearness and distance can reveal questions that established members take for granted.

items.prompt: Why may an aging person become a stranger even to themselves?
options: A legal change of name or nationality erases all prior identity
All autobiographical memories disappear at the same age
Longstanding witnesses to shared meanings and life history become fewer
Retirement automatically removes every past occupational identity
items.answer: Longstanding witnesses to shared meanings and life history become fewer
items.explanation: The loss of consociates and co-biographers can weaken the relational basis of continuity in one's biography.

items.prompt: How did GOH's illness become an interpersonal crisis?
options: The patient role overshadowed other identities and reorganized her support convoy
Her family and colleagues remained unaware, so every relationship stayed unchanged
All previous relationships immediately returned to normal after treatment
The illness unfolded independently of timetables, roles, and social ties
items.answer: The patient role overshadowed other identities and reorganized her support convoy
items.explanation: Illness interrupted expected participation and shifted the centrality of people in her network.

items.prompt: What exclusion occurred during RAS and Dan's first adoption?
options: Both men automatically received identical legal recognition and parental leave
Federal law already recognized their relationship as a marriage
RAS was recognized as the adoptive parent while Dan was excluded from the hearing
Interracial adoption was mandatory, leaving them no choice of family form
items.answer: RAS was recognized as the adoptive parent while Dan was excluded from the hearing
items.explanation: Dan was treated as a household member. The essay also describes parental leave limited to mothers who had physically given birth.

items.prompt: Why does marriage recognition matter directly for aging in RAS's account?
options: It equalizes health and life expectancy across all married couples
It organizes rights and decisions that matter in later life
It prevents the onset of illness in parents
It removes geographical distance from family networks
items.answer: It organizes rights and decisions that matter in later life
items.explanation: Legal recognition shapes interdependent rights and decisions that become particularly consequential in later life.

items.prompt: How does historical time reach into individual lives?
options: Only through policies currently in force in a given calendar year
By giving all people born in one year identical experiences
Only through crises the individual personally witnessed
Through one's own cohort and the experiences of close family generations
items.answer: Through one's own cohort and the experiences of close family generations
items.explanation: The authors describe historical experiences transmitted through shared meanings, habits, and interdependent relationships.

items.prompt: How did the demographic transition alter the meaning of finitude in the essay?
options: It confined death to childhood
It increasingly linked death to the end of a long life
It eliminated every relationship between age and death
It made all cohorts understand death identically
items.answer: It increasingly linked death to the end of a long life
items.explanation: The essay contrasts an earlier sense of death as possible at any age with its later association with old age.

items.prompt: Which account of the epidemiological transition and gender matches the essay?
options: Changing causes of death made all illness experiences identical across genders
Gendered illness experiences operate outside historical circumstances
Women's relationships are explained entirely by timeless biology
They connect gendered illness patterns with relational worlds
items.answer: They connect gendered illness patterns with relational worlds
items.explanation: The discussion links mortality and morbidity patterns to demographic change, bodies, caregiving, and opportunities for long relationships.

items.prompt: Which statement captures both sides of interdependence?
options: It provides support and continuity while exposing plans to others' health and functioning
Having more relatives automatically removes uncertainty and policy dependence
It is merely an inferior developmental stage before independence
It includes only present exchanges and excludes long-term reciprocity
items.answer: It provides support and continuity while exposing plans to others' health and functioning
items.explanation: Relationships can be protective resources and sources of contingency; reciprocal obligations may also span decades.

items.prompt: What do the authors criticize in active-aging discourse?
options: Every possible benefit of exercise or social participation
Institutional support for accessible community activities
An active/passive division that can turn limitations and dependence into failure
Older people choosing and adapting activities to their own circumstances
items.answer: An active/passive division that can turn limitations and dependence into failure
items.explanation: Such dichotomies can obscure capacities and contributions retained by people labeled ill, disabled, or dependent.

items.prompt: Which account best reflects the disability perspective discussed in the essay?
options: A diagnosis alone determines participation
Every older person needs the same environmental adaptation
Functioning reflects capacity in relation to environment
Disabled and non-disabled people form two entirely separate categories
items.answer: Functioning reflects capacity in relation to environment
items.explanation: The relational view asks how environments allow or prevent the use of capacities, rather than locating everything within an individual impairment.

items.prompt: How do the authors interpret their vanguard experiences?
options: They ask whether strategies developed through boundary crossing may help with aging
They prove that vanguards require no institutional support in later life
They conclude that stigma invariably strengthens every support network
They restrict new life-course pathways to women alone
items.answer: They ask whether strategies developed through boundary crossing may help with aging
items.explanation: The discussion combines difficulties in maintaining convoys with questions about resilience. It does not establish a universal advantage.

options: Assigning one certain future lifespan and health level to every cohort
Projecting how current changes may shape future cohorts' relationships and aging options
Restricting analysis to detailed records of past family history
Excluding lived experience and relying only on aggregate demographic prediction
items.answer: Projecting how current changes may shape future cohorts' relationships and aging options
items.explanation: The agenda maps possible consequences of demographic, policy, and cultural change for future interpersonal worlds.
